Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, the next step that will unblock an accurate PoC is a technical deep-dive where we review your current inference topology and map the migration/PoC plan (model variants, KV cache behavior, batching, and network constraints).

High-level goals for the session:
- Surface current provider / self-hosted differences that affect latency & throughput
- Confirm model sizes / token patterns + expected RPS during peak tests
- Agree on data handling (retention, residency) and security checklist for the Private option
- Outline concrete deliverables for the PoC (SOW scope, success criteria, telemetry hooks)

Proposed slots (60–75 min):
- Tue Aug 10 — 9:00–10:15 AM PT
- Wed Aug 11 — 11:00 AM–12:15 PM PT
- Thu Aug 12 — 2:00–3:15 PM PT

I've attached a short migration scope and risk matrix to help frame the conversation (acme_migration_scope.pdf, redwood_poc_risks.xlsx). Could you confirm which slot works and who from your infra/security team should join? If those windows don't work, share two alternatives and we'll re-align.

Thanks — looking forward.

All — I can present the migration path and runtime differences. Draft pre-call checklist below (will attach a formatted checklist to the calendar invite):

Pre-call checklist (requested from Acme):
- Current provider: instance types (GPU SKU), node counts, and autoscaling policy
- Model variants in use (base, quantized variants, fp16/INT8) and approximate sizes per variant
- Typical request pattern: average tokens per request, tail length, and burst RPS
- Any on-prem / VPC networking constraints (eg, whitelisted IPs, egress rules)
- Sample logs/trace for a 10-min peak window (anonymized)

Also, Marissa/Monica — I’ll cover KV cache migration implications and what we will need for routing/fallbacks during the PoC. I propose we keep the engineering deep-dive to 90 min so we don’t rush the KV/cache section.

I’ll prepare a short slide pack and a checklist PDF to attach to the invite.
